title: A Life-Course Conceptual Model of Stigma in Adults With Tourette Syndrome: Implications for Nursing Science

publication_dates.publisher_status: Publish Ahead of Print; Original Article
publication_dates.date_caveat: Crossref registration/deposit timestamps are not exact first-publication times. Newly returned since prior scan; first-publication date in overlapping day does not establish exact within-day ordering.

novelty: Absent from October15 retrieved set and current primary ledger; three default-branch identifier/title searches returned zero. No claim of independently new cohort.
design: Qualitative interview study informing a conceptual model
population: 34 adults with Tourette syndrome; exact age distribution, tic severity, persistence, comorbidity, geography, sampling and eligibility not verified.
exposure: Participants' accounts of social stigma; no assigned intervention
outcome: Interpretive interview themes and conceptual model; no validated quantitative outcome effect extracted.
original_summary: Participants described stigma shaping identity, relationships and employment, with coping, concealment and withdrawal among responses. This directly addresses adult social and functional burden.
followup: No prospective follow-up verified; a life-course framing is not proof of longitudinal observation.
adverse_events: Not a treatment trial; no treatment safety estimate.
attrition: Recruitment flow, refusals, incomplete interviews and analytic sample accounting unverified.
risk_of_bias: Recruitment, interview methods, coding framework, reflexivity, saturation, negative cases and triangulation require full-methods verification. Qualitative accounts do not estimate prevalence, causal effects or intervention benefit.
applicability: Adult burden is directly relevant; representation of persistent severe tics, pain and co-occurring conditions remains unknown. No pediatric-to-adult extrapolation is needed for the sampled adults, but wider adult generalization is unestablished.
cohort_overlap_status: Unverified; do not call independent replication.
claim_supported: A 34-adult qualitative report offers stigma-related themes for research planning.
claim_not_supported: Population prevalence, validated prediction, causal life-course effects, efficacy of proposed nurse-led support, tic reduction, durable benefit, disease modification or cure.
retrieval_status: Official NCBI EFetch abstract/date metadata and publisher public abstract/overview inspected; Crossref dates corroborate October15. Web extractor could not read the PubMed/DOI/Ovid article; standard HTTP retrieved publisher overview. Main methods and supplement not inspected. No source text copied into deliverables.
reviewer: Research assistant extraction; not independent clinical peer review
correction_retraction_check: No linked notice in PubMed, no update-to/relation notice in inspected Crossref response, focused PubMed notice query zero. Exact-DOI web notice search yielded only irrelevant matches; not a complete publisher/Crossmark audit.
next_verification_task: Verify lawful methods/supplement for recruitment, severity/comorbidity coverage, analytic rigor and cohort overlap before promoting model-specific claims or planning a new study.
